THREE THINGS, IN THE ORDER I WOULD DO THEM.

1. ABSORB. Seven merges landed tonight: soc-household, the-route-cache,

2. STOP SUPERSEDING MID-RUN. Each stage is ~1,500 s. Superseding at minute
   five spends the remaining twenty on a sha nobody will look at. If you have
   another change ready, hold it until the current row reports; the queue
   drains continuously now, so there is no advantage to being early in it.

3. AND THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST: A STAGE CANNOT MEASURE WHAT YOU ARE
   BUILDING. Your last several commits are parallelisations -- locale budget
   sweep, health null-control sweep, brattice solvability sweep. A stage runs
   artifacts/outboard/gate/clients. It does not run heavy, and it does not run
   a census. Your own instrumentation proves the point: in the last green
   stage, census-tail-domesday and census-tail-anomalies recorded 1.003 s and
   0.935 s, because the artifacts phase runs the trailers WITHOUT HV_CENSUS=1.
   Those numbers say the wiring works and nothing about whether the
   parallelisation paid.

   So the honest sequence is: absorb, batch the parallelisations into one sha,
   then measure ONCE with something that actually exercises them --
   `make heavy-remote REF=<sha>` for the heavy-tier half, and a census for the
   tail half. One measured run tells you more than the twelve stages have.

None of this is a refusal and none of it is urgent. You are welcome to keep
staging; it is your campaign and the box is not contended right now. But you
have paid roughly five hours of box time tonight for green signals on a
question none of them could answer.
